population.note: FICTIONAL. There are about 276M adults. Current users are 34.9%, about 96.3M. Ever-users are 47.5%, about 131.1M, up 7.5 points against a limit of 9.4. That leaves 12.6% (≈34.8M) who used and are off now, and ≈144.9M who have never used. Cycling arithmetic: about 18.5 points of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5.0 points of the off-now group restarted at least once before stopping again, so (18.5 + 5.0)/47.5 ≈ 49.5%. That fits the inherited ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% one-year restart, and daily orals make stopping and restarting easier. Age check: 18–29: 19% × 52M = 9.9M; 30–49: 40% × 92M = 36.8M; 50–64: 50.5% × 62M = 31.3M; 65+: 26% × 70M = 18.2M. Total ≈ 96.2M ≈ 34.9%. The 65+ band grew more slowly (21→26%) because the bone wave pushed about one in four older ever-users onto a medically advised pause or a permanent stop. Of the 18.2M users aged 65+, ≈15.8M are Medicare-paid and ≈2.4M pay through retiree plans, cash or imports. Income thirds average (37 + 35.5 + 32.2)/3 = 34.9. The bottom third grew most (+7.7), mainly through $149–249 cash pills and imports, not coverage. The off-now 34.8M include ≈3.1M who lost coverage when employers exited for the 2036 plan year and did not move to cash, ≈2.6M older users on bone pauses or post-fracture stops, and ≈1.9M on long self-directed 'grey' holidays. Pediatric use is 1.2% of ≈73M ≈ 880k, mostly adolescents 12+. Uptake slowed after the 2035 adolescent bone-accrual readout. Nearly half of US children now live with at least one parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The statutory terms of the permanent Part D obesity benefit are unchanged: $199/month negotiated rate, $50 copay, counselling visit, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. Medicare pays 18.0% of fills, ≈17.3M users (≈15.8M aged 65+ and ≈1.5M disabled under-65): ≈7.0M for diabetes and ≈10.3M for obesity. Obesity-benefit spend: 10.3M × $199 × 12 ≈ $24.6B gross. Beneficiaries pay 10.3M × $50 × 12 ≈ $6.2B, leaving ≈$18.4B for the program. All Medicare incretin fills: 17.3M × $199 × 12 ≈ $41.3B gross. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC use the 90% match and the continuation standard, and no state joined or left. Medicaid pays 13.0% of fills, ≈12.5M users × $199 × 12 ≈ $29.9B gross before supplemental rebates. Commercial net prices have now fallen toward the public rate, so the fixed $199 no longer looks generous. It is close to what everyone else pays.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including generic oral semaglutide. The Telangana first-filer plant's import alert stands. China: generic semaglutide, tirzepatide copies, and 'research' retatrutide vials, with Chinese API underlying most gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–75/month. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt also have generics. US: rival filers' mid-2035 contingent dates passed with no launch because a court stayed FDA's forfeiture decision against the first filer (see events).
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline. Under renewed direct-portal commitments and PBM deals from Jan 2035: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $199–249 direct (down from $249–329); Wegovy pill 50 mg $249 (from $299); oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) unchanged at $149–150; retatrutide $399 direct and $1,349 list (from $449/$1,649); amycretin $449; MariTide $499/month-equivalent. PBM net ≈$175–190 and average US net ≈$182, down ~9%. Payer mix of ≈96.3M users: commercial 28.4% (27.4M); Medicare 18.0% (17.3M); Medicaid 13.0% (12.5M); cash/direct 31.0% (29.9M, including ≈4.9M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers); imported/counterfeit 9.6% (9.2M). Sum = 96.3M = 100.0%. Employer retreat: 49% of employers cover for weight management, down from 64%. Commercial users fell only 1.6M because most plans that left still pay under diabetes, established-cardiovascular (semaglutide CV label) and sleep-apnea codes. About 85% of remaining weight-management plans are gated and a third have tenure gates. Daily orals are ≈55% of users, up from ≈36%. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, ≈4.9M subscribers, with churn now high)
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial completed enrolment; no filing)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gray-market 'research' retatrutide among gym and physique users
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new approvals and no new indications this step. The oral_parity driver continues to be met by an existing product, the 50 mg Wegovy pill approved Feb 2034 at 16.4% versus 16.1% injectable. What changed is uptake: with the pill at $249 and the starter at $149, daily orals passed half of users in 2035. Parity is still with injectable semaglutide, not with tirzepatide or 12 mg retatrutide. Lilly's next-generation orals entered phase 3 in 2035 and are not filed. Survodutide's MASH sNDA got a complete response letter in Aug 2035 asking for outcome histology. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide, a muscle-preserving combination in phase 3 with no prior filing, was filed in Mar 2036 on 72-week data showing lean mass ~10% of loss versus ~35%. Under standard review a decision cannot come before 2037. Incretin market ≈$205B in 2036. US ≈$190B: ≈87.1M paying users (96.3M − 9.2M imports) × ≈$182 average net × 12 ≈ $190.2B. Ex-US ≈$15B and eroding to generics. Volume growth outweighs the price fall.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Self-directed dose holidays add re-escalation nausea episodes.
Absolute numbers keep rising with the larger user base and the 65+ population.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Gray product still confounds reporting.

Now recognised as a population problem. ≈2.5M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims, up from 1.6M. Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50. The Oct 2035 Sentinel and Medicare analysis links ≥3 years' use in untrained over-65s to a measurable decline in gait speed and grip strength.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Feb 2036: FDA class Warnings and Precautions statement on lean-mass and bone-density loss across all incretin products, including low-dose orals, with baseline body-composition assessment recommended for users over 50. Not boxed. A joint AGS/Endocrine Society/ASBMR guideline recommends resistance training, ≥1.2 g/kg protein and DEXA for all users over 50. CMS annual DEXA requirement for long-term 65+ users unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈10.0M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 10.0M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 21,000 excess hip fractures a year, against ~310,000 US total. At ~$40k acute-plus-rehab cost each, 21,000 × $40,000 ≈ $0.84B a year, mostly Part A and Medicare Advantage and unscored. The vertebral tail among cycling women 50–64 is now the most cited figure in backlash material. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks as mobile vans multiply.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Folded into the Feb 2036 class warning; bone endpoints required in all filings; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; FDA requested a pragmatic fracture-outcomes trial. The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. At ~4 per 100,000 baseline among ≈96M users: 96.3M × 0.00004 × 0.7 ≈ 2,700 excess cases a year, mostly partial and permanent loss of vision in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: May 2034 class Warnings and Precautions statement and Medication Guide update stand. MDL consolidated in 2035 with bellwether trials set for 2037.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 2032 retatrutide data stand (~12% versus ~5%). A Mar 2036 Pew survey finds 37% of current users say they have felt 'flattened' at some point and 31% take planned dose holidays. That is self-report with no comparator. An NIH-funded randomised low-dose trial began enrolling in 2035 with readout in 2038.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC consent orders stand. No label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Employer exits for the 2036 plan year pushed ≈3M people off coverage at once. Most moved to cash pills or imports, but ≈3.1M stopped.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code softens it for Medicare. The Seventh Circuit still has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users and in cash or import users with no clinical contact. Vitamin D and protein insufficiency are now cited as bone-wave cofactors.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Covered by the 2036 joint guideline; the Part D counselling template screens for it. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent readout shows a smaller gain in BMD Z-score than placebo (about −0.2 SD at 2 years) of uncertain lasting significance. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Adolescent labels updated with bone-accrual data in late 2035; postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Import users rose more slowly, from ≈7.1M to ≈9.2M, as cash prices fell. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are up a further ~25% since 2034, now driven more by tablets than vials. No contamination cluster on the 2033 scale has occurred.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA import alerts expanded to seven exporters. The 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled. Individuals still not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. Pressed counterfeit 50 mg Wegovy-pill and Foundayo tablets are the main gray product, at 0–300% of labelled content. Hypoglycaemia in insulin users and GI emergencies dominate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP verified-pharmacy guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use remain ~20% above matched non-users. Sarcopenia and monocular vision loss are both cited cofactors.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. Pooled DEXA cohorts confirm more visceral fat and less lean mass at the same weight after two or more cycles, concentrated in over-50s cut off by coverage loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Cited in the 2036 joint guideline and the FDA class warning text; no separate action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mean resting heart-rate rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide; arrhythmia significance unclear.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precautionary label; CV outcomes trial ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Loss of functional independence in long-term older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Medicare Advantage plans report rising home-health and assisted-transfer claims among untrained 75+ users with ≥3 years' use and ≥15% loss. Effect size is unsettled, and heavier non-users have their own frailty.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Under the FDA fracture-trial request; no separate action.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Weekend or fortnight 'grey holidays' followed by restart at full dose produce vomiting, dehydration and occasional acute kidney injury. ED coding is poor, and Foundayo's shorter half-life makes holidays more common on it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Medication Guide reminder to re-titrate after missed doses; no new action.

food_and_beverage.state: With about 35% of adults on the drug, salty-snack volume falls ~3% a year and confectionery ~4%. Declines are slowing as the user base saturates and backlash 'heritage' brands market the full table. Bone-forward fortified dairy and protein lines are the growth category, now with a 'with your DEXA' calcium/D/protein code on pack. Discount grocers sell cheap protein shakes and 'regain-friendly' value packs. Unregulated 'nature's GLP-1' supplements (berberine, fibre, 'incretin teas') pass ~$3B in sales.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits volume decline. Beer is down and NA formats hold. Bars in Austin and Nashville report drinking concentrated on Fridays and Saturdays as 'holiday weekend' users come back, a small on-premise offset to the decline.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and spend per cover is ~12% below 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced bowls are standard on weekdays, and 'holiday menus' with full portions run on weekends. Church-linked catering and potluck halls in Memphis and Houston grow with the backlash.

apparel.state: The 'structured' and 'cycle' split holds. Elastic three-size 'cycle' lines are now the volume segment in discount chains. A small 'Whole Body' fat-positive label revival, mainly women 50–64 in the Midwest, takes plus-size floor space back at two mid-market chains.

fitness.state: Growing on the bone wave. Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' benefits are now offered by most large MA plans, mobile DEXA capacity is up ~40%, and strip-mall strength studios for over-60s multiply. Corporate gym subsidies shrink as employers retreat. Qualified older-adult trainers are still the bottleneck.

insurance.state: Employer retreat: 49% of employers cover for weight management, down from 64%, and most of those that left keep coverage only under diabetes, cardiovascular and sleep-apnea codes. 'Code shopping', meaning claims for sleep studies and cardiology workups, rises. Pharmacy trend falls to ~+4%. Life insurers price untreated BMI ≥30 and now also low DEXA in older applicants. Fracture and fall costs land on Part A and Medicare Advantage.

pharma.state: Volume up ~23% and average net down ~9%. US revenue rises modestly to ≈$190B. Novo's 50 mg pill is the volume leader and gives Novo back the share lost in the 2033 pen recall. Lilly leads on revenue through retatrutide and tirzepatide. Amgen's MariTide grows among coached top-third users. The bimagrumab filing is the sector's bet on the bone wave. Indian and Chinese makers dominate ex-US and the parcel trade.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income, as before, with a new reading of age. Trained, DEXA-verified shoulders mean a coached regimen. A soft 'pill body' means cash or a coded commercial plan. In over-60s, a stoop, a cane, or a thin wrist in a splint now reads as 'the bone wave', and people in that group are the most likely to say they regret the drug.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use converges (bottom 32.2% against top 37%), but the bottom third reaches the drug through $149 starter pills and imports with no DEXA and no coach, so bodies still diverge. Women 50–64 who cycled are the group the vertebral tail falls on and the group leading the backlash. In Dayton, Ohio, a 'Regain Is Not Failure' group that began in a Kettering church basement holds regular meetings across Montgomery County.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first weekday meals among users; full-table weekends among holiday-takers and the off. In Memphis a network of Black congregations running 'Whole Table' Sunday dinners has become the visible face of a religious and fat-positive revival. It frames shared, unmeasured eating as fellowship and is explicitly not anti-medicine for diabetics.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps add 'holiday weekends' to the on/off/pausing field. 'Unmedicated' grows from niche to a recognisable identity among under-30s, the age band with the lowest use. Profiles citing DEXA results read as boasting.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Contested again. The backlash is visible and has three loose wings: a fat-acceptance revival (NAAFA membership roughly doubles), a 'natural' wellness-populist wing selling supplements and distrust of pharma, and a religious wing. In Jun 2036 the Southern Baptist Convention adopted a resolution warning against 'pharmaceutical contentment' while affirming medical treatment. Still, most Americans who can afford the drug take it.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Pew (Mar 2036): 37% of ≈96M current users (~36M) report having felt 'flattened' at some point and 31% (~30M) take planned dose holidays. This is self-report, not diagnosis. The 2032 retatrutide figure (~12% versus ~5%) is still the only controlled estimate. Roughly 9M Americans are on top-dose triple or dual regimens, which implies about 630k excess clinically meaningful anhedonia cases if the association is causal. The ≈4.9M 'calm' subscribers remain unmeasured, with annual churn near 50%.
interior_life.framing: A side effect everyone talks about, managed by everyone at home. 'The grey' is ordinary vocabulary. 'Foundayo Fridays' (skipping the short-half-life pill for the weekend) and 'holiday fortnights' are discussed the way people once discussed skipping a beer. Prescribers say 'reward modulation' and warn about re-titration. 'Calm' brands still sell the feeling, under FTC limits and two class warnings.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Many employers that dropped weight coverage also removed 'focus' from lifestyle catalogues, so 'metabolic tenure' persists only where gated plans remain. Sales, hospitality and creative staff openly schedule holidays before pitches and launches. Managers are coached not to ask. Unions now bargain to keep coverage at all rather than over its gates.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'grey era' has become a target of parody. A 2035 late-night sketch about a man scheduling his feelings for Saturday became a catchphrase. 'Written on holiday' displaces 'written unmedicated' as the Nashville badge. Weekend leisure intensifies: festivals, spicy-food events and Saturday-only bars.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex is scheduled around holidays: couples report 'Saturday people' and 'weekday people'. Therapists screen for holiday patterns, and the re-escalation nausea on Mondays has become a joke in its own right. Couples in which one partner joined a backlash group and the other is coached describe the drug as a values dispute.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: In the 2036 campaign the drug shows up as complaint, not as policy. Candidates of both parties talk about employer retreat and 'bone-wave grandparents'. Wellness populists court the backlash with supplement-friendly rhetoric. The Safe Pens bill and import legalisation are still stalled, and no government action resulted.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and enforcing. It added the Feb 2036 class warning on lean mass and bone, issued the survodutide MASH complete response letter, declared the first-filer's forfeiture (now stayed by a court), expanded import alerts, and requested a fracture trial. It still brings no individual prosecutions. Congress has passed no importation or authentication law, and FTC consent orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Unchanged since 2032: permanent Part D obesity benefit at the $199 statutory rate with a $50 copay; 90% Medicaid match for the 31 states plus DC on the continuation standard. No new state action, no mandate, and no federal response to employer retreat.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged: ≥80% PDC, verified six-monthly weights, 5% response or clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, 90-day bone-pause code, and two misses suspend coverage for 6 months. Indiana and Arkansas keep their 12-month rules. Private conditioning shrinks because employers are exiting, not loosening. Remaining gated plans keep kiosk weights and tenure gates. Cash users are ungated and unmonitored, so the cohort with the least clinical contact is growing fastest.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide, which stays covered under the OSA code even where weight coverage ended. Large fleets keep voluntary visual-field checks. Army accession policy is still contested; Air Force waivers continue.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply the world and the 9.2M-user US gray market, now mostly tablets. Section 232 tariffs remain. The Telangana import alert and the forfeiture litigation are standing bilateral irritants with India.

events.event: Novo and Lilly sign renewed direct-portal and PBM price commitments: maintenance injectables fall to $199–249 a month, the 50 mg Wegovy pill to $249, and retatrutide list to $1,349. Oral starter doses stay at $149–150 and the Medicare $199 rate is untouched

Several Fortune 100 employers and the two largest benefits administrators announce they will end weight-management coverage for the 2036 plan year and keep incretins only under diabetes, established cardiovascular disease and sleep-apnea codes. A year-end employer survey puts weight-management coverage at 49%, down from 64%

A federal district court stays FDA's May 2035 ruling that the Telangana first filer forfeited its 180-day generic exclusivity. Rival filers' mid-2035 contingent launch dates pass with no US generic semaglutide, and the appeal is argued at the D.C. Circuit in 2036 without a ruling

A Pew-style national survey finds daily pills are now the majority route for incretin users, and that 31% of current users take planned dose holidays to escape 'the grey'. 'Foundayo Fridays' enters common usage

Citing a Sentinel and Medicare analysis of about 21,000 excess hip fractures a year and 2.5 million sarcopenic long-term users, FDA adds a class warning on lean-mass and bone-density loss to every incretin label and asks for a fracture-outcomes trial. In March, Lilly files its muscle-preserving bimagrumab–tirzepatide combination, with a decision not before 2037

The Southern Baptist Convention adopts a resolution warning against 'pharmaceutical contentment', weeks after a 'Regain Is Not Failure' and Whole Table march in Memphis draws an estimated 15,000. NAAFA reports its membership has doubled since 2034

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide hinges on a D.C. Circuit ruling on the stayed forfeiture. Meanwhile ≈9.2M Americans use imported or counterfeit product, mostly pressed tablets of variable content, and Congress has passed neither import legalisation nor authentication.

Employer retreat has split access into a coded tier (diabetes, CVD, sleep apnea, Medicare, Medicaid) and a cash tier of ≈30M people with no gating, no DEXA and no counselling. That cash tier is now the fastest-growing cohort, just as the bone wave makes monitoring matter most.

The bone wave argues for pauses and the regain data argue against them. The cheap daily pill makes both lifelong use and casual holidays easier. About 21,000 excess hip fractures a year are billed to Part A and Medicare Advantage, unscored, while the muscle-preserving fix will not get an FDA decision before 2037 and will not come cheap.

'The grey' is a mainstream complaint managed by self-directed dose holidays. Nobody controls those holidays, and their effects on body composition, NAION risk and re-escalation harm are unmeasured until the low-dose RCT reads out in 2038.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, including the 90-day 'bone pause' code, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
The FTC consent orders stand: 'calm' and 'focus' brands may not claim to treat anxiety, and the 'Safe Pens' authentication bill is still stalled in Congress.

prose.headline: The Pill Won. Your Employer Quit. Now Count Your Bones: America at 35% on GLP-1s
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 a little more than a third of American adults take an incretin drug, and most of them swallow it. The fifty-milligram Wegovy pill, approved in 2034 as an equal of the weekly shot, became the default once its price fell to $249 and the starter dose stayed at $149. More people now take the drug as a pill than as an injection. Pens are for people chasing the strongest results, retatrutide or Amgen's monthly MariTide, and for the coached clients of Scottsdale and Buckhead who can pay for them.

Prices fell the dull way. There was no generic flood. Novo and Lilly renewed their portal commitments, the pharmacy-benefit managers cut deals, and maintenance prices slid by about fifty dollars. Generic semaglutide is still not on American shelves. The FDA ruled that the Indian company holding the first right to launch had forfeited it, a federal judge stayed the ruling, and the mid-2035 date rivals had circled came and went. An appeals court heard the case this year and has not ruled.

Employers have started leaving. Paying even falling prices for a third of the workforce indefinitely turned out to be more than many could stomach. For the 2036 plan year several of the largest companies stopped covering weight loss and kept the drug only for diabetes, heart disease and sleep apnea. Fewer than half of employers now cover it for weight. Cardiology and sleep clinics report a run of referrals that billing staff call code shopping. Of those who lost coverage, most moved to cash, some moved to imported tablets of uncertain strength, and about three million stopped. Medicare and the thirty-one Medicaid states did not move. Their $199 rate and their weigh-in rules are what they were in 2032, and the fixed price that once looked generous is now roughly what everyone else pays.

This was the year the muscle and bone losses stopped being a footnote. A federal analysis of Medicare claims put the excess at about twenty-one thousand hip fractures a year and counted two and a half million long-term users with clinical muscle wasting. In February the FDA put a warning on lean-mass and bone loss on every incretin label and asked for a fracture trial. Geriatric and bone societies now tell anyone over fifty on the drug to lift weights, eat protein and get a scan. Mobile scanning vans park outside Krogers. Medicare Advantage plans pay for strength classes. Lilly filed a combination designed to preserve muscle, which cannot be approved before 2037. The fracture bills go to the part of Medicare that does not buy the drug, and nobody has added them up.

The complaint everyone used to whisper is now ordinary talk. People call it the grey. A third of users say they have felt it, and about as many take planned holidays from the drug. Lilly's pill, Foundayo, clears the body fast enough that skipping it Friday brings appetite and something like pleasure back by Saturday night. Bars in Austin notice the weekends. Emergency rooms notice the Mondays, when people restart at full dose and vomit.

The backlash can be seen in the street. In Memphis, Black congregations running Whole Table Sunday dinners marched with women from Dayton's Regain Is Not Failure groups, many of them in their fifties and sixties who cycled through coverage loss and are carrying the vertebral fractures. The Southern Baptist Convention warned against pharmaceutical contentment. Fat-acceptance groups doubled their membership. Supplement sellers market berberine as nature's version. None of this has changed a law. In the presidential campaign both parties talk about grandparents with broken hips and companies that walked away, and neither has proposed anything.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Lorraine Pruitt takes the pill at 5:40 with four ounces of water and stands at the counter for thirty minutes because the box says to. She uses the time to pack her husband's lunch. Ray stopped in March when the school district's plan dropped weight coverage. His A1c was 6.1, a tenth short of the code. Lorraine's is 6.1 too.

She used to take the fifty. Now she takes the starter, $149 on the portal, and she is regaining slowly.

At the bus depot she dispatches twenty-two routes. Her coworker Tamika keeps a blister pack of Indian tablets in her purse and says the lot number checks out on the Telegram list. Lorraine says nothing.

At lunch the mobile DEXA van is parked outside the Kroger on Wilmington Pike. The technician is twenty-four and kind. The T-score is minus 2.1. He hands her a sheet with a resistance band printed on it and a QR code for a Medicare strength class she can't join for seven years.

Her daughter Keisha texts: Skipping my Foundayo this weekend, come Sunday? Mama's making the greens.

The Regain Is Not Failure group meets Thursday in the Kettering church basement. Lorraine has gone twice. She liked the coffee and did not like the speeches.

At dinner she eats half a pork chop and sets the other half aside for Ray. He eats it without looking up.

Before bed she stands on the connected scale out of habit, though no one reads it anymore. 191. She steps off and steps back on, and it says 191 again.
